prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Houston for AC repair?
answer_verbatim:
I can help — but “best” depends on exactly where you’re located in Houston and what you value (fast same‑day service, lowest price, long warranty, work on a specific brand, etc.). A quick way I can help right now:

1) Quick clarifying questions
- What ZIP code or neighborhood are you in?
- Is this an emergency (no cooling right now)? Do you need same‑day service?
- Do you prefer a big local company, a small independent tech, or a national chain?
- Is the unit under warranty or a specific brand model?

2) If you want immediate troubleshooting (before booking)
- Check the air filter — replace if dirty.
- Confirm thermostat is set to “cool” and temperature set lower than room temp.
- Make sure circuit breaker to the AC isn’t tripped.
- Clear debris from around the outdoor condenser and ensure the fan runs.
- If you hear grinding, loud bangs, or smell burning — turn the unit off and call a pro.

3) How to pick the best HVAC company in Houston
When comparing companies, look for:
- Valid licensing and insurance (ask to see proof).
- NATE‑certified technicians or manufacturer training.
- Clear, written estimates and diagnoses (not just “will call back with price”).
- A parts and labor warranty (30–90 days minimum; better companies offer 1 year+).
- Good recent reviews on Google/Yelp/BBB and responsive customer service.
- Transparent service fees and flat-trip/diagnostic fees explained upfront.
- Availability for after‑hours or emergency service if you need it.

4) Questions to ask a company when you call
- Are you licensed and insured? Can you provide license number?
- How long have you been servicing Houston?
- Do you guarantee your work and for how long?
- Will I get a written estimate before any repair?
- Are your technicians NATE certified or manufacturer trained?
- Do you offer emergency/same‑day service and what is the additional cost?

5) Typical repair cost ranges (approximate)
- Thermostat replacement: $100–$300
- Capacitor or contactor: $150–$500
- Refrigerant recharge (minor): $150–$500
- Fan motor or blower repairs: $300–$900
- Compressor replacement or major repairs: $1,200–$3,500+
(Actual cost depends on unit age, brand, exact problem, and parts availability.)

If you tell me your ZIP code and whether you need same‑day service, I’ll give a short list of well‑reviewed HVAC companies in your area plus a recommended first call and a sample script to use on the phone.
